_doc: Monotone ratchet for scripts/check-ontology-wired.mjs. Each counter is the number of ontology legs that are declared but not yet behaviour: `staged` schemes awaiting their wave, and `n/a` gate/tool/hook legs carrying a written reason. A counter may fall freely; a rise fails the gate. There is no --allow-increase flag — raising a number means hand-editing this file in the same PR as the row that needs it, so the new number lands in the diff beside its justification.
_measured: 2026-09-02, 21 schemes: 14 active and wired, 7 staged with dated expiries (MS wave 3; SRC wave 5; UC/TT/RB/FS/EP wave 8). CANON and E were corrected from staged to active once the gates that already enforced them were found — the first survey overstated how much of the ontology was ungoverned. Each wave lowers staged; none may raise it. | 2026-09-03 wave 2: naHook 16 -> 17 for the new ARC scheme. Raised by hand, as this file requires: an arc42 slot is prose under a heading, not a schema'd artifact, so post-edit-artifact-schema.mjs has nothing to validate at edit time and a hook would be ceremony. scripts/check-arc42-slots.mjs is the enforcement, wired on both tracks. | 2026-09-05 wave 8: naHook 17 -> 18 for TT. Raised by hand, as this file requires. TT named post-edit-artifact-schema.mjs until this wave taught the meta-gate to check whether a named hook COVERS the row's SSOT — and it never could: that hook validates a JSON or YAML document against a JSON Schema, and TABLETOP-SCENARIOS.md is prose with a bespoke parser. So the leg was never behaviour; the rise records a claim withdrawn, not a claim abandoned. The same coverage check found three other rows (MS, SRC, UC) naming that hook with nothing in its table to match them; MILESTONES.yml was covered for real in this wave (a new `yaml` extract mode), and SRC and UC are staged, so their claims must become true before they go active. TT went active, so staged falls 7 -> 6 and the floor drops with it. | 2026-09-05 wave 8, UC goes active: naTool 5 -> 6 and naHook 18 -> 19, both hand-raised, both recording a claim WITHDRAWN rather than abandoned. UC declared `arbiter graph build` as its tool and post-edit-artifact-schema.mjs as its hook; neither was ever true — no CLI verb reads use cases (the USECASE graph node does not exist yet, so naming that verb was the phantom-command class of claim), and the hook's dispatch table covers this path on neither track, which the coverage check added earlier in this same wave now refuses to let a row assert. staged falls 6 -> 5 as UC goes active.
